title: Introduction to HTTP and APIs

content.intro: This lesson introduces Introduction to HTTP and APIs using the supplied syllabus terms, a visual map, and a short inspectable example.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding Introduction to HTTP and APIs helps you make JavaScript behavior explicit instead of relying on guesswork. The skill becomes more valuable as programs combine data, user input, runtime APIs, and failures.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Introduction to HTTP and APIs is one of the named concepts in the JavaScript syllabus. Focus on the behavior it defines, the inputs that influence that behavior, and the result you can observe. JavaScript language semantics are specified by ECMAScript; browser and Node.js APIs belong to their host runtimes, so check which environment a feature requires.

content_blocks.title: Build the idea in small steps

items.title: Requests and responses
items.text: Connect Requests and responses to Introduction to HTTP and APIs. Define the expected behavior first, demonstrate it with a small example, and explain one edge case before using it in a larger program.

items.title: HTTP methods and status codes
items.text: Practise HTTP methods and status codes with the smallest example that demonstrates the syntax, then change one input to see which part of the result changes.

items.title: Headers and content types
items.text: Connect Headers and content types to Introduction to HTTP and APIs. Define the expected behavior first, demonstrate it with a small example, and explain one edge case before using it in a larger program.

items.title: JSON APIs
items.text: Apply JSON APIs in the browser host environment. Check that the required element/API exists, handle failure states, and test keyboard use, network errors, and narrow viewports where relevant.

content_blocks.run_instructions: This example is an inspectable teaching snippet, not an arbitrary-code execution service inside CodeLeaf. Save it as a small .js file and run it with a supported Node.js release for console-only examples, or place browser-only code in an HTML page with the required element. Compare the actual output with the expectation and change one input at a time.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial snippet, remove temporary logging, and repeat with one boundary or invalid input.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: First, name the expected result for Introduction to HTTP and APIs. Then trace the code one statement at a time: record the important value before and after each operation, and check whether the output matches your expectation. Change one input or condition; if the result is different, inspect that step instead of rewriting the whole program.

content_blocks.title: Environment and correctness note
content_blocks.text: The ECMAScript 2026 edition is the stable language reference used by this course. The browser DOM, Fetch API, and Node.js APIs are host features. Emerging proposals and runtime support can change; verify compatibility before depending on a feature in production.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small program that demonstrates Introduction to HTTP and APIs. Use at least one of the listed subtopics (Requests and responses), include one normal input and one edge case, and write two sentences explaining why the observed result makes sense.
task_acceptance_criteria: The program uses the lesson concept accurately and has readable names.
The learner states the expected result and checks the actual result.
At least one edge case, failure path, or environment assumption is addressed.
hints: Reduce the program to the smallest example that still shows the concept.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without understanding its input and output.
common_mistakes.why: A memorized example can appear to work while hiding assumptions about input values or runtime.
common_mistakes.fix: Explain the expected output first, run the smallest example, and test one boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming browser APIs are part of core JavaScript.
common_mistakes.why: ECMAScript does not define the browser DOM or Node.js filesystem APIs.
common_mistakes.fix: Identify the host environment and consult its official API reference.

common_mistakes.why: Several simultaneous edits make the cause of a behavior difficult to isolate.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one variable or line, reproduce the result, and record what changed.

summary: Introduction to HTTP and APIs describes a specific behavior or tool that should be tested with an observable example.
